279797062_33751aaa.text: The anterior thalamic nuclei (ATN), a Papez circuit component, encompass the anterodorsal (AD), anteroventral (AV), and anteromedial (AM) thalamic nuclei. Structurally, the ATN facilitate communication among the neocortex, hippocampus, amygdala, and hypothalamus. Functionally, they play pivotal roles in learning, memory, spatial navigation, and goal-directed behaviors

279797062_6369b05f.text: . We found specific morphological and topological features characterize all ATN neurons, including a small number of primary dendrites (3.8 ± 0.1), absence of local axons, and elaborate, tufted distal dendrites with spines. Thus, all ATN neurons are thalamocortical projection neurons but can be grouped into larger classes based on dendrite morphology

279797062_de94e1f6.text: . Overall, the resulting 13 ATN neuron types are highly distinct from each other in their brain-wide input-output connections. Their outputs target one to six cortical and hippocampal regions, compared to one to two non-cortical regions, except AD1, which projects to one cortical, one hippocampal and four non-cortical regions. Most project to combinations of prelimbic, anterior cingulate, retrosplenial, visual, orbital and entorhinal cortical areas, while a minority project to hippocampal and parahippocampal structures including the subiculum, parasubiculum and postsubiculum
279797062_de94e1f6.section: Shared cellular properties of excitatory projection neurons across ATN

279797062_049553b3.text: . Specifically, the AV contains AV1, AV2 and AV3 neuron types, while the AD contains AD1 and AD2 types. The AM contains the most neuron types, with AM1, AM2 and AM3 in all portions and ADP, AMd, AMv, AMdc and AMV in their corresponding topographic domains
279797062_049553b3.section: Shared cellular properties of excitatory projection neurons across ATN

279797062_79c8b7ec.text: . First, the AD contains two highly distinct neuron types: AD1 and AD2. AD1 neurons are located in dorsolateral AD and project to postsubiculum, laterodorsal visual area, laterointermediate visual area, and subcortical mammillary regions. AD2 neurons are located in the ventromedial AD and project to retrosplenial, visual, postsubicular, and subcortical mammillary regions. Second, the AV contains three unique neuron types: AV1 neurons are located in dorsomedial AV and project to prelimbic, anterior cingulate, and anterior retrosplenial areas. AV2 neurons are found in ventrolateral AV and project to granular retrosplenial and ventral visual stream areas. AV3 neurons are found in dorsolateral AV and project to both prefrontal and visual cortical areas. Third, the AM contains at least eight connectionally distinct neuron types. AM1 neurons are found throughout the nucleus and project to cingulate and retrosplenial cortices. AM2 neurons are found in ventrolateral AM and project to prefrontal cortex, area prostriata, and ventral visual stream areas. AM3 neurons are found throughout the nucleus and project to prefrontal, cingulate and retrosplenial cortices. Other AM types include ADP neurons (dorsal aspect of the posterior AM) that project to prelimbic, cingulate, and visual cortices; AMd neurons (dorsal aspect of the middle AM) that project to cingulate and visual cortices; AMv neurons (ventral aspect of the middle AM) that project to prelimbic and cingulate cortices; AMdc neurons (rostral aspect of the AM dorsal cap) that project to prelimbic and cingulate cortices; and AMV neurons (caudal aspect of the AM ventral border) that project to ventral orbital, agranular insular and entorhinal cortices

279797062_289edc65.text: . Within the AM, Tnnt1 labels two distinct populations, one in the principal AM and another in the AM dorsal cap. We show that this selective labeling corresponds to different pathway-defined cell types, such that Tnnt1+ principal AM neurons correspond with AM3, while Tnnt1+ dorsal cap neurons correspond with AMdc. The most ventral AMV neuron type is also selectively labeled by Col5a1, while the dorsally located ADP is labeled by Cacna2d1, and at least one more broadly distributed AM cell type is distinguished by Calb1

279797062_d062691f.text: . Using these molecular markers, we were able to define all pathway-defined ATN types, except AM1. Although all types analyzed in this study are glutamatergic and likely derive from common progenitors, their connectional distinctions are associated with marked differences in specific molecular markers and local morphological features.
